transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Since my in-laws moved into our house, I’ve been constantly keyed up and exhausted. I’m snapping at my wife, putting off calls I’d normally handle right away, and I almost let one of my musician’s contracts fall apart because I just couldn’t think straight.
How long ago did your in-laws move in, and how long have you been feeling this keyed up and exhausted?
About a month now. It really started when my in-laws moved into the house.
Can you tell me more about your sleep—are you having trouble falling asleep or staying asleep at night?
I’m not really sure. I just know I’ve been exhausted; I haven’t paid close attention to whether it’s trouble falling asleep or waking up during the night.
Aside from the stress about your in-laws living with you, do you find yourself worrying excessively about other things too, like work, finances, or your health?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed whether I’m worrying about other things like that.
Besides feeling keyed up and exhausted, have you noticed feeling sad, down, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’ve been feeling down or not enjoying things.
Thinking about the last few weeks, have you found yourself losing interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy, like your music work or spending time with your wife?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to whether I’m enjoying those things less lately.
In the past month, have you had any periods where you felt sad, hopeless, or tearful, even briefly?
I can’t really say. I haven’t noticed specific times like that, at least not enough to be sure.
Have you noticed feeling physically tense, restless, or on edge—like you can't sit still or your muscles feel tight—since your in-laws moved in?

Yeah. Since they moved in, I’ve been constantly keyed up and worn down. I’m snapping at my wife, putting off calls I’d normally handle right away, and I almost let a musician’s contract fall apart because I couldn’t think straight.
Do you notice this keyed-up, tense feeling even in situations that have nothing to do with your in-laws or the home situation—like when you're out with friends or focused on an unrelated task?

It mostly feels tied to the situation at home. Since my in-laws moved in, I’ve been keyed up all the time, and it spills over into work—I avoid calls I’d usually take right away, and I nearly let a musician’s contract fall apart because I couldn’t think straight.
